items.title: Integer abelian structure and rank by finite reduction
items.statement: Every subgroup of Z^n is free of rank at most n. Every subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finitely generated. Every finitely generated abelian group M is Z^r direct-sum a finite sum of Z/d_j Z with d_j>1. Its torsion subgroup is exactly the finite summand, and r is independent of the decomposition. A surjection between finitely generated abelian groups with finite kernel preserves r.
items.strategy: Use only finite choices. For K<=Z^n project to the last coordinate. Its image is dZ by the published cyclic-subgroup lemma. If d=0 reduce the ambient rank; if d>0 choose v in K projecting to d. Subtract the uniquely determined multiple of v from each element of K, obtaining K=Zv direct-sum ker(projection|K). Induction proves finite freeness. For a subgroup of M use its inverse image under a fixed surjection Z^n->M. Next take a finite basis of the kernel of this surjection as columns of an integer matrix. Swaps, sign changes and addition of an integer multiple of one row or column to another have explicit inverse operations and preserve the quotient up to isomorphism. Move a nonzero entry to the first pivot and make it positive. A nondivisible entry in its row or column gives, by division with remainder and a swap, a smaller positive pivot. If the pivot divides its row and column, clear these; if it fails to divide a remaining entry, add that entry's row to the pivot row, then perform column division to lower the pivot. Well-ordering terminates these descents. Once the pivot divides the entire rectangle, clear its row and column and recurse on the smaller rectangle. The resulting diagonal gives Z^n/K as the stated cyclic sum by coordinate quotient maps and the first isomorphism theorem. Unit entries give zero summands, missing pivots give infinite cyclic summands, and empty/zero matrices are included. No prime-power splitting or general PID theorem is needed. Every finite cyclic quotient has precisely the residues 0,...,d-1 by integer division, so its sum is finite; the free part is torsion-free by integer cancellation. Define V(M)=Hom_groups(M,(Q,+)) with pointwise rational vector operations. Evaluation on the displayed free generators identifies V(M) with Q^r because every map kills torsion, and arbitrary rational generator values extend uniquely. Finite-dimensional independence bounds make r intrinsic. For a surjection f:M->N with finite kernel, every map M->Q kills the kernel: a finite-order element has zero image in Q. Hence precomposition gives a rational-linear bijection V(N)->V(M), proving rank invariance. These arguments also prove a finitely generated torsion abelian group is finite and a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group is free.

items.title: Commutator product identities in the fixed convention
items.statement: For [x,y]=xyx^-1y^-1 and conjugation by u meaning uvu^-1: [x,yz]=[x,y] y[x,z]y^-1 and [xy,z]=x[y,z]x^-1[x,z]. In a central commutator pairing both arguments are multiplicative, including negative powers.
items.strategy: Expand each product and cancel; derive inverse and integral-power cases explicitly. Define left-nested simple commutators, with a one-fold commutator equal to its argument.

items.title: The three-subgroup containment for normal subgroups
items.statement: For normal A,B,C in G, [[A,B],C] is contained in [[B,C],A][[C,A],B].
items.strategy: Establish the Hall–Witt identity by direct cancellation in the repository convention; pass to the quotient by the normal product on the right. Expand products of commutator generators to extend the element identity to subgroup containment. Do not cite an unbuilt Hall–Witt theorem.

items.title: Lower-central commutators add weights
items.statement: [gamma_i(G),gamma_j(G)] <= gamma_{i+j}(G) for all i,j>=1. Modulo gamma_{i+j+1}, the induced commutator pairing of the two lower-central factors is well-defined and biadditive.
items.strategy: Induct on i, uniformly in j, applying the three-subgroup containment to gamma_i,G,gamma_j. Product identities dispose of choices of representatives, conjugation errors and negative exponents.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)

items.title: Finite generation of lower-central factors
items.statement: If G is generated by a finite S, gamma_i/gamma_{i+1} is abelian and generated by the images of the finitely many i-fold simple commutators in S and their inverses. If G is nilpotent, every gamma_i is finitely generated.
items.strategy: Induct on i using product expansions modulo the next term. Descending induction from gamma_{c+1}=1 lifts factor generators to generators of each term. Finitely generated does not mean torsion-free.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)

items.title: Subgroups of finitely generated nilpotent groups are finitely generated
items.statement: Every subgroup K of a finitely generated nilpotent G is finitely generated.
items.strategy: Apply the local integer-abelian lemma to the abelian base. Intersect K with the lower-central series; each intersection factor embeds into a finitely generated abelian factor, so is finitely generated by that lemma. Lift these finite generating sets through the finite series.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)

items.title: Finite torsion and the torsion-free quotient
items.statement: In a finitely generated nilpotent G the finite-order elements form a finite characteristic subgroup T, and G/T is torsion-free nilpotent.
items.strategy: For closure under products use induction on class: for class c>=2, <b,gamma_2(G)> is normal and has class at most c-1, since its commutator subgroup lies in gamma_3(G). For torsion a,b of order(a)=m, (ab)^m is a product of conjugates of b in the torsion subgroup of this smaller-class group. Handle class one separately. The subgroup T is finitely generated by the preceding lemma; its lower-central abelian factors are finitely generated torsion groups and hence finite. If (gT)^n=T then g^n has finite order, so g has finite order.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)
references.locator: Lemma 10.46, Theorem 10.47, Proposition 10.48, Corollaries 10.49 and 10.52, printed pp.287–288

items.title: Upper-central factors of a torsion-free nilpotent group
items.statement: If a nilpotent group has torsion-free center, every Z_{i+1}/Z_i is torsion-free and the group is torsion-free.
items.strategy: A nonzero coset in Z_2/Z_1 is detected by yZ_1 -> [y,g] in Z_1 for some g. These maps are homomorphisms by centrality, so Z_2/Z_1 is torsion-free. Apply induction to G/Z_1 and use Z_i(G/Z_1)=Z_{i+1}(G)/Z_1. Spell out correct ascending indices; the draft has index typos.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)

items.title: Integral coordinates from a central cyclic refinement
items.statement: A finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent group has a finite central series with infinite cyclic nontrivial factors, and chosen ordered lifts give a bijection Z^m -> G by ordered products. Here m is the length of the chosen refinement.
items.strategy: Refine each finite-rank free abelian upper-central factor by its ordered basis. Lift the refinement to G; every refined factor remains central. Prove existence and uniqueness of ordered exponents by successive quotient projections. These integral coordinates need not be adapted to the unisolated lower central series; do not assign lower-central weights to this refinement without a separate argument.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)
references.locator: Lemma 10.51, printed p.288; central-factor refinement derived locally

items.title: Bass–Guivarc’h dimension and nilpotent Hirsch length
items.statement: For finitely generated nilpotent G of class c let r_i be the free rank of gamma_i/gamma_{i+1}; set D(G)=sum i*r_i and h(G)=sum r_i. Empty sums are zero for G=1.
items.strategy: Use the local integer-abelian lemma: r_i is the intrinsic number of infinite cyclic summands, equivalently dim_Q Hom(gamma_i/gamma_{i+1},Q). This defines nilpotent Hirsch length only; no assertion about arbitrary polycyclic series or generic PID rank uniqueness is imported.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)

items.title: Lower-central generators, residue coordinates and weighted length
items.statement: Choose an ordered invariant-factor generating list in each gamma_i/gamma_{i+1} and lifts u_ij in gamma_i. Infinite-factor exponents are integers; an order-d factor uses 0<=a<d. The weight is i. For a normal coordinate tuple let its integer weighted length be the least R>=0 such that every infinite exponent has |a_ij|<=R^i and every nonzero residue forces R>=1. Define Q(R) using all residues and |a_ij|<=R^i, R>=1. Also define weighted word counts before normalization.
items.strategy: Fix product order increasing in i, then in j. Distinguish a generating list of factors, a redundant lcs alphabet, and an integral Malcev basis. For G with torsion the first torsion-free coordinate model will be G/T; finite kernel representatives must be retained when returning to G.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)

items.title: Finite normal quotients preserve lower-central ranks
items.statement: For finite normal F in finitely generated nilpotent G, D(G/F)=D(G) and h(G/F)=h(G). For H=gamma_c(G), the earlier lower-central factors of G/H agree with those of G, so D(G/H)=D(G)-c*r_c.
items.strategy: Induction on commutators proves q(gamma_i G)=gamma_i(G/F). The kernel on factor i equals the image of F intersect gamma_i in gamma_i/gamma_{i+1}: if x=f*y with x in gamma_i, f in F and y in gamma_{i+1}, then f=x*y^-1 lies in gamma_i. This kernel is finite. Apply the local integer-abelian finite-kernel rank lemma. For H=gamma_c, identify each factor i<c by the quotient isomorphism.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)
references.locator: Theorem 14.26 reduction, printed p.511; the exact rank verification is supplied locally

items.title: Finite normal quotients preserve ball growth
items.statement: For finite generating S of G, finite normal F and q:G->G/F, |B_{qS}(n)| <= |B_S(n)| <= |F| |B_{qS}(n)| for every n>=0.
items.strategy: The image of the source ball equals the target ball by lifting words of length at most n. Each fiber contains at most |F| elements. Give these cardinality inequalities explicitly rather than relying on quasi-isometry alone; that would require a later growth-invariance theorem.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)
references.locator: Theorem 14.26 finite-kernel reduction, printed p.511; direct fiber-count proof

items.title: Finite lower-central coordinate systems with torsion accounted for
items.statement: For every finitely generated nilpotent G, first form Q=G/T(G). Q has integral coordinates along a central cyclic refinement and also unique ordered lower-central coordinates with bounded residues in any finite cyclic factors. The same mixed lower-central construction works in G; corresponding factors of G and Q have the same free rank r_i, so both have exactly r_i unbounded exponents of weight i. All choices are finite.
items.strategy: Explicitly quotient finite torsion before invoking the torsion-free integral model. Then construct the mixed lower-central form by successive projection in both G and Q. Prove equality of the layer ranks directly: the quotient map is onto on every lower-central factor and its kernel is the image of the finite set T(G) intersect gamma_i, so finite-kernel rank preservation applies. Prove uniqueness by successive projection; do not identify the two coordinate systems. Return to G either with its own mixed form or with a finite T representative.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)

items.title: Finite collection alphabets include commutators and torsion carries
items.statement: A finite lower-central generating alphabet can be enlarged finitely to contain commutators of its letters and the powers carrying finite-order factor generators into deeper lower-central terms.
items.strategy: Starting with finitely many chosen letters, at each stage add commutators with all previous letters and required finite-order powers. Each new operation raises the lower-central depth; a branch has length at most c, with finite branching. Include inverses and omit the identity from weight assignments. Record the fixed replacement words for changing an arbitrary layer list to an invariant-factor list.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)

items.title: Weighted collection with finite-order carries
items.statement: Fix G of class c and a mixed lower-central coordinate system. For each lambda>=1 there is C depending only on these data and lambda such that every word with at most lambda R^i letters of assigned weight i, R>=1, has normalized free exponents of weight j bounded by C R^j, and bounded residue exponents. If its value lies in gamma_k, all earlier layer coordinates vanish and the remaining representation uses only weights at least k. In particular a length-n word has coordinate bounds C max(1,n)^j.
items.strategy: Collect one layer at a time in the ambient lower-central filtration. Moving a weight-i letter past a weight-j letter creates errors only in weights >=i+j. For O(R^i) such moves, the weight-j error estimate is a finite sum of terms binom(O(R^i),s) O(R^(j-si)), with j-si>=1, hence O(R^j). Fixed torsion carries move O(R^i) letters to deeper weight and preserve the bound. Prove this recurrence for each phase, including negative exponents and fixed basis replacements; induct on the ambient layer, never replace gamma_k(G) by its own lower-central filtration. Termination follows from increasing depth. Apply the bound to concatenations and reversed inverse words as well.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory (837-page edition)
references.locator: Lemma 14.21 and Proposition 14.25, pp.505–508,510–511; retain the last-layer conclusion only from part II

items.title: Power compression in the last lower-central term
items.statement: For G finitely generated nilpotent of class c>=1, each fixed z in gamma_c(G) satisfies |z^m|_S <= C_z |m|^(1/c) for every nonzero integer m; z^0=1.
items.strategy: Induct on class for all groups at once. Generate gamma_c by finitely many [s,u] with u in gamma_{c-1}. Write m=a q^(c-1)+b with q=ceil(m^(1/c)), 0<=b<q^(c-1), 0<=a<=q. In G/gamma_c, induction gives words v,w of length O(q) representing u^(q^(c-1)) and u^b modulo gamma_c. Since gamma_c is central, [s,u]^m=[s^a,v][s,w]. Negative m follows by inversion, and finite products by centrality. The constants are uniform in m, not necessarily in z.

references.title: Druţu–Kapovich, Lectures on Geometric Group Theory (585-page draft)

items.title: Both bounds for last-term weighted distortion
items.statement: Let G have class c>=1 and H=gamma_c(G). With finite word metrics there is C>=1 such that C^-1 |h|_H^(1/c)-C <= |h|_G <= C |h|_H^(1/c)+C for all h in H. If H is infinite, Delta(n)=max{|h|_H: h in H, |h|_G<=n} is bounded above and below by positive multiples of n^c for all sufficiently large n. If H is finite, Delta is bounded.
items.strategy: Collection gives |h|_H <= C max(1,|h|_G)^c, since only the last layer remains. Decompose H as Z^r plus finite torsion, apply power compression to the fixed free basis, and bound the finite part. For the lower distortion bound choose powers of one infinite basis generator, with exponent a sufficiently small multiple of n^c. State explicitly that finite last terms have no positive-power lower bound.

references.locator: Proposition 14.20 and Lemma 14.21, printed pp.504–508 (finite last terms handled separately locally)

items.title: Coordinate boxes and word balls have matching size
items.statement: For mixed lower-central coordinates on G, there are a,b>0 with Q(a n) contained in B_S(n) contained in Q(b n) for all sufficiently large integers n. For real R>=1 use floor(R^i) in each free coordinate; |Q(R)| is the product of (2 floor(R^i)+1) over all free coordinates, times the product of all finite cyclic orders. Thus |B_S(n)| is bounded above and below by positive multiples of n^D(G).
items.strategy: Upper inclusion is collection. For the lower inclusion prove Q(R) subset B_S(CR) by induction on class. In G/H with H=gamma_c choose a short lift w of the projected element using the induction hypothesis. The weighted word for w^-1 g has O(R^i) letters in layer i; collection and vanishing lower coordinates bound its H length by O(R^c). Last-term compression makes this correction O(R). The abelian base is a finite product of integer intervals with bounded residues. If H is finite use its diameter; constants absorb all small radii. Count via uniqueness; do not count redundant commutator alphabets as independent coordinates.

references.locator: Proposition 14.25 and Theorem 14.26, pp.510–512; two-sided box inclusion proved by the stated local induction

items.title: The Bass–Guivarc’h growth degree formula
items.statement: For every finitely generated nilpotent group G and every finite generating set S, constants 0<c_S<=C_S exist with c_S n^D(G) <= |B_S(n)| <= C_S n^D(G) for all integers n>=1. This includes finite groups with D=0 and is independent of S at the level of polynomial degree.
items.strategy: Apply the preceding box theorem and adjust constants for finitely many small radii. Explain alternatively the class induction: quotient by H=gamma_c, count disjoint translated H-ball intersections for the lower bound and at most one bounded H-ball per quotient fiber for the upper bound. The finite-normal lemma and rank lemma justify the torsion reduction. State no limit |B(n)|/n^D and no generating-set-independent asymptotic coefficient.

items.statement: For H=UT_3(Z), write matrices (a,b,c) with product (a+a',b+b',c+c'+ab'). Then gamma_2={(0,0,c)}, gamma_3=1, so r_1=2,r_2=1 and D=4.

items.title: Torsion-free does not mean torsion-free lower-central factors
items.statement: False claim: every lower-central factor of a torsion-free nilpotent group is torsion-free. The subgroup G of UT_3(Z) with entries (a,pb,c), for fixed p>=2, refutes it: G is torsion-free and G/[G,G] is Z^2 direct-sum Z/p.
